title: Advanced usage
text: md_grob() converts markdown text grid graphics object (grob).

title: Advanced usage
code: gr <- md_grob("This is **bold** and *italic* text.")  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
text: Control position x, y, hjust, vjust:
code: grid.newpage()  gr1 <- md_grob("**Top left**", x = 0, y = 1, hjust = 0, vjust = 1) gr2 <- md_grob("*Center*", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5) gr3 <- md_grob("`Bottom right`", x = 1, y = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0)  grid.draw(gr1) grid.draw(gr2) grid.draw(gr3)

title: Advanced usage
text: Use width enable line wrapping:
code: long_text <- "This is a **long text** that will be automatically wrapped across multiple lines using the `width` parameter."  gr <- md_grob(long_text, x = 0.1, hjust = 0, width = 3)  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
text: chunks_grob() converts ‘flextable’ paragraph objects grobs. Use need superscripts, subscripts, custom colors.
code: chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("E = mc"),   as_sup("2") )  gr <- chunks_grob(chunks)  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
code: chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("The speed of light is "),   as_b("c"),   as_chunk(" = 3\u00D710"),   as_sup("8"),   as_chunk(" m/s") )  gr <- chunks_grob(chunks)  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
code: chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("Normal "),   colorize(as_chunk("Red "), color = "red"),   as_highlight(as_chunk("Yellow bg"), color = "yellow") )  gr <- chunks_grob(chunks)  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
text: Use default_text_props() customize font size, family, color:
code: props <- default_text_props(   font_size = 14,   font_family = "serif",   font_color = "darkblue",   code_font_family = "mono" )  gr <- md_grob("Custom **styled** text with `code`", text_props = props)  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
text: Text properties can also set globally via ‘flextable’:
code: set_flextable_defaults(   font.size = 14,   font.color = "darkblue" )  gr <- md_grob("Text using **flextable** defaults")  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr) # Reset defaults init_flextable_defaults()

title: Advanced usage
text: Use standard markdown image syntax:
code: img_path <- system.file("img", "Rlogo.png", package = "png")  text_with_img <- sprintf("The R logo: ![](%s) in text.", img_path)  gr <- md_grob(text_with_img) #> Warning: Image file not found. #> ✖ Cannot find file .  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
text: Use as_image() explicit size control:
code: img_path <- system.file("img", "Rlogo.png", package = "png")  chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("The R logo "),   as_image(src = img_path, width = 0.3, height = 0.3),   as_chunk(" is iconic.") )  gr <- chunks_grob(chunks) #> Warning: Image file not found. #> ✖ Cannot find file .  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
text: img_baseline_ratio parameter controls vertical image alignment: 0: Image bottom text baseline 0.15: (default) Similar text descent proportions 0.35: Image centered text vertical center 0.5: Image centered baseline
code: props <- default_text_props(img_baseline_ratio = 0.35)  gr <- md_grob(   sprintf("Text ![](%s) centered", img_path),   text_props = props ) #> Warning: Image file not found. #> ✖ Cannot find file .  grid.newpage() grid.draw(gr)

title: Advanced usage
text: Use annotation_custom() add grobs ggplot2:
code: library(ggplot2)  stats_grob <- md_grob(   "**R\u00B2 = 0.87**\n\n*p < 0.001*",   hjust = 0,   vjust = 1 )  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +   annotation_custom(     grob = stats_grob,     xmin = 25, xmax = 35,     ymin = 4.5, ymax = 5.5   )

text: Use as_paragraph_md() markdown table cells: Sepal Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species 5.1 3.5 1.4 0.2 setosa 4.9 3.0 1.4 0.2 setosa 4.7 3.2 1.3 0.2 setosa

title: Font recipes
text: Using fonts ‘munch’ involves two independent steps: Measurement, ‘munch’ calls gdtools::strings_sizes() compute text metrics (width, ascent, descent). hood, ‘systemfonts’ locates font file, Cairo calculates metrics. font registered via systemfonts::register_font(), gdtools::register_gfont(), gdtools::font_set(), gdtools::font_set_liberation() gdtools::font_set_auto() found measurement time. Rendering, graphic device draws text. device way resolving font names. mismatches happen: font measurement found may invisible device, vice versa. steps find font, output correct. disagree, text positioned using one font’s metrics drawn another ; leading overlapping, clipping misaligned labels.

title: Font recipes
text: Devices ragg, svglite ggiraph use ‘systemfonts’ measurement rendering. Every registered font visible sides. simplest approach font_set_liberation(), registers Liberation Sans, Serif Mono single call, internet needed, SIL Open Font License: system-aware detection (Arial, Helvetica, etc. Liberation fallback), use font_set_auto(): specific fonts (e.g. Google Font), use font_set():
code: library(gdtools) font_set_liberation() font_set_auto() library(munch) library(ggplot2)  fonts <- font_set(sans = font_google("Open Sans"))  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   labs(title = "**Open Sans** via *font_set()*") +   theme_minimal(base_family = fonts$sans) +   theme(plot.title = element_md())

title: Font recipes
text: Cairo devices (cairo_pdf(), png(type = "cairo")) use Cairo engine rendering ‘gdtools’ uses measurement. However, font lookup differs: measurement goes ‘systemfonts’, rendering goes fontconfig. Fontconfig scans system-installed fonts. means: System fonts (e.g. Arial, Helvetica), measurement rendering agree. Everything works. Google Fonts via register_gfont(), found measurement necessarily fontconfig, depending cache . Liberation fonts via font_set_liberation() (individual register_liberation*()), found measurement . Rendering falls back silently unless fonts also installed OS level. Use font_family_exists(system_only = TRUE) check whether font found fontconfig:
code: library(gdtools)  # Found by measurement (systemfonts + registry)? font_family_exists("sans") #> [1] TRUE  # Found by fontconfig (system-installed only)? font_family_exists("sans", system_only = TRUE) #> [1] TRUE

title: Font recipes
text: Standard devices (pdf(), png(), jpeg()) use font engine ignore ‘systemfonts’ entirely. ‘munch’ uses ‘gdtools’ (relies Cairo) text measurement. standard pdf() device uses font engine. output correct, fonts used ‘munch’ must also known pdf(). ‘extrafont’ package bridges gap: imports TrueType fonts R’s PDF device generating font metric files pdf() can use. key requirement: every font used plot must available ‘systemfonts’ (measurement) pdf() (rendering). font registered ‘systemfonts’ pdf(), text metrics match rendering output positioning errors.

title: Font recipes
text: steps : Install fonts system level, “Arial” “Courier New” must installed system fonts. Import fonts extrafont::font_import(), scans system fonts creates metric files pdf(). needed . Load fonts session extrafont::loadfonts(), registers imported fonts pdf() current session. Disable device check options(munch.skip_device_check = TRUE), since ensured font concordance manually, warning longer needed. Note: cairo_pdf() simpler alternative. uses Cairo rendering (engine ‘gdtools’ measurement), system-installed fonts work without ‘extrafont’. Use pdf() + ‘extrafont’ cairo_pdf() available.
code: library(gdtools) library(munch) library(ggplot2)  df <- data.frame(   x = 1:3,   y = 1:3,   label = c("**Bold**", "*Italic*", "`Code`") )  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, label = label)) +   geom_label_md(code_font_family = "Courier New") +   theme_minimal(base_family = "Arial")  # Make Arial and Courier New available to pdf() library(extrafont) # font_import() # Run font_import() once to scan system fonts, # then loadfonts() in each session. loadfonts()  # Suppress the device warning since we ensured font concordance options(munch.skip_device_check = TRUE)  pdf(file = "munch-example.pdf", width = 7, height = 7) print(p) dev.off()

title: Font recipes
text: text looks wrong (wrong font, misaligned labels), cause almost always measurement/rendering disagreement. quick checklist: font found measurement? FALSE: font registered ‘systemfonts’. Register register_gfont(), font_set(), systemfonts::register_font(). font found device? Cairo devices: FALSE: font system-installed. Either install OS level switch ‘systemfonts’ device (ragg, svglite). pdf(): check extrafont::fonts() includes family. ragg/svglite/ggiraph: step 1 passed, always works. sides find font? Even find font, may file (e.g. different weight substitution). Compare:
code: gdtools::font_family_exists("My Font") gdtools::font_family_exists("My Font", system_only = TRUE) # What systemfonts resolves systemfonts::match_fonts("My Font")  # What's installed at the system level subset(systemfonts::system_fonts(), family == "My Font")

title: Using munch with ggplot2
text: element_md() replaces element_text() render markdown titles, subtitles, captions, axis labels.   advanced markdown rendering (images, spans, custom CSS), see also marquee::element_marquee().
code: ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   labs(     title = "**Fuel Consumption** vs *Weight*",     subtitle = "Data from the `mtcars` dataset",     caption = "Source: *Motor Trend* (1974)"   ) +   theme(     plot.title = element_md(size = 16),     plot.subtitle = element_md(size = 12),     plot.caption = element_md(size = 9)   ) ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   labs(     x = "Horsepower (*hp*)",     y = "Miles per gallon (**mpg**)"   ) +   theme(     axis.title.x = element_md(),     axis.title.y = element_md()   )

title: Using munch with ggplot2
text: element_chunks() uses ‘flextable’ formatting functions (as_paragraph(), as_chunk(), etc.) build rich text superscripts, subscripts, colors, highlighting, features markdown support.

title: Using munch with ggplot2
text: Build text combining chunks inside as_paragraph():
code: chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_b("Bold"), as_chunk(", "),   as_i("italic"), as_chunk(", "),   as_chunk("x"), as_sup("2"), as_chunk(", "),   as_chunk("H"), as_sub("2"), as_chunk("O") )  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   theme(plot.title = element_chunks(chunks))

title: Using munch with ggplot2
text: Superscripts subscripts essential scientific text. element_chunks() makes straightforward:  Chemical formulas:  Units exponents:
code: title_chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("Analysis: "),   as_b("R"), as_sup("2"),   as_chunk(" = 0.87, "),   as_i("p"), as_chunk(" < 0.001") )  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +   theme(plot.title = element_chunks(title_chunks)) subtitle_chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("Concentration of "),   as_b("H"), as_sub("2"),   as_b("SO"), as_sub("4"),   as_chunk(" in solution") )  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   theme(plot.subtitle = element_chunks(subtitle_chunks)) caption_chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("Units: mol\u00B7L"), as_sup("-1"),   as_chunk(" | Speed: m\u00B7s"), as_sup("-2") )  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   theme(plot.caption = element_chunks(caption_chunks))

title: Using munch with ggplot2
text: colorize() as_highlight() add color background highlighting:
code: title_chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("Results: "),   colorize(as_chunk("significant"), color = "#E63946"),   as_chunk(" difference") )  subtitle_chunks <- as_paragraph(   as_chunk("Compare "),   as_highlight(as_chunk(" Group A "), color = "yellow"),   as_chunk(" vs "),   as_highlight(as_chunk(" Group B "), color = "cyan") )  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   theme(     plot.title = element_chunks(title_chunks),     plot.subtitle = element_chunks(subtitle_chunks)   )

what: Text annotations with geom_text_md() and geom_label_md()
title: Using munch with ggplot2
text: geom_text_md() geom_label_md() render markdown-formatted labels directly plot, similar geom_text() geom_label().  geom_label_md() adds background rectangle better readability:
code: annotations <- data.frame(   x = c(15, 25, 30),   y = c(4, 3, 2),   label = c("**Group A**", "*Group B*", "`Group C`") )  ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +   geom_text_md(     data = annotations,     aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),     size = 4   ) ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +   geom_point() +   geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +   geom_label_md(     label = "**R\u00B2 = 0.75**\n\n*p < 0.001*",     x = 28, y = 5,     hjust = 0, vjust = 1,     fill = "white",     label.padding = unit(0.5, "lines")   )

title: Create a Grob from flextable Chunks — chunks_grob
text: Creates grob directly flextable chunk data.frames (created flextable::as_paragraph()), bypassing markdown parsing.

title: Create a Grob from flextable Chunks — chunks_grob
code: chunks_grob(   chunks,   x = 0.5,   y = 0.5,   hjust = 0.5,   vjust = 0.5,   width = NULL,   line_spacing = 1.2,   img_baseline_ratio = 0.15,   name = NULL )

title: Create a Grob from flextable Chunks — chunks_grob
text: chunks chunk data.frame flextable (e.g., flextable::as_paragraph()). x X position (0-1 npc units). y Y position (0-1 npc units). hjust Horizontal justification. vjust Vertical justification. width Maximum width inches (NULL wrapping). line_spacing Line height multiplier. img_baseline_ratio Controls vertical alignment inline images. Specifies proportion image height text baseline: 0 = bottom baseline, 0.15 = default, 0.35 = centered text, 0.5 = centered baseline. name Grob name.

what: Default Text Properties for Markdown Grobs — default_text_props
title: Default Text Properties for Markdown Grobs — default_text_props
text: Returns list text properties used rendering markdown text. Default values taken flextable::get_flextable_defaults(), allowing integration flextable's theming system providing standalone API munch.

title: Default Text Properties for Markdown Grobs — default_text_props
code: default_text_props(   font_size = NULL,   font_family = NULL,   font_color = NULL,   code_font_family = NULL,   line_spacing = NULL,   img_baseline_ratio = NULL )

title: Default Text Properties for Markdown Grobs — default_text_props
text: font_size Font size points. font_family Font family name regular text. font_color Text color. code_font_family Font family name inline code (backticks). Defaults "mono". line_spacing Line height multiplier. img_baseline_ratio Controls vertical alignment inline images. Specifies proportion image height appears text baseline: 0: image bottom baseline 0.15: (default) similar text descent proportions 0.35: image centered text vertical center 0.5: image centered baseline

title: Default Text Properties for Markdown Grobs — default_text_props
text: list class "text_props" elements: font.size: Font size points font.family: Font family name font.color: Text color code.font.family: Font family code line_spacing: Line height multiplier img_baseline_ratio: Image baseline alignment ratio element names use dot separators (font.size, font.family, etc.) compatibility 'flextable' conventions. Function parameters newer elements use snake_case (line_spacing, img_baseline_ratio) preferred convention going forward.

title: Default Text Properties for Markdown Grobs — default_text_props
text: arguments NULL (default), values inherited flextable::get_flextable_defaults(). allows users either: Use munch independently specifying properties:   Use flextable's theming system:
code: props <- default_text_props(font_size = 12, font_family = "serif") md_grob("**bold**", text_props = props) flextable::set_flextable_defaults(font.size = 14) md_grob("**bold**")

title: Default Text Properties for Markdown Grobs — default_text_props
code: library(grid)   # Get current defaults default_text_props() #>  #> ── Text properties  #> • font_size: 11 #> • font_family: "DejaVu Sans" #> • font_color: "black" #> • code_font_family: "mono" #> • line_spacing: 1.2 #> • img_baseline_ratio: 0.15  # Override specific properties default_text_props(font_size = 14, font_color = "navy") #>  #> ── Text properties  #> • font_size: 14 #> • font_family: "DejaVu Sans" #> • font_color: "navy" #> • code_font_family: "mono" #> • line_spacing: 1.2 #> • img_baseline_ratio: 0.15  library(gdtools) font_set_liberation() #> Font set #>   sans:    Liberation Sans [liberation] #>   serif:   Liberation Serif [liberation] #>   mono:    Liberation Mono [liberation] #>   symbol:  Liberation Sans [liberation] #>   4 HTML dependencies  # Specify a monospace font for inline code props <- default_text_props(   font_family = "Liberation Sans",   code_font_family = "Liberation Mono" )  if (require(ggiraph, quietly = TRUE)) {   x <- girafe(     width_svg = 2,     height_svg = 1,     bg = "wheat",     options = list(opts_sizing(rescale = FALSE)),     code = {       grid.newpage()       gr <- md_grob("Text with `inline code`", text_props = props)       grid.draw(gr)     },     dependencies = list(       liberationsansHtmlDependency(),       liberationmonoHtmlDependency()     )   )    print(x) }

title: Markdown Theme Element for ggplot2 — element_md
text: theme element renders text labels markdown. Use place ggplot2::element_text() plot titles, subtitles, captions, axis labels, etc.

title: Markdown Theme Element for ggplot2 — element_md
code: element_md(   family = NULL,   code_font_family = NULL,   face = NULL,   colour = NULL,   size = NULL,   hjust = NULL,   vjust = NULL,   angle = NULL,   lineheight = NULL,   color = NULL,   margin = NULL,   debug = FALSE,   inherit.blank = FALSE )

title: Markdown Theme Element for ggplot2 — element_md
text: family Font family. code_font_family Font family inline code. Defaults "mono". face Font face ("plain", "bold", "italic", "bold.italic"). colour, color Text color. size Font size points. hjust Horizontal justification (0-1). vjust Vertical justification (0-1). angle Text rotation angle degrees. lineheight Line height multiplier. margin Margins around text (use ggplot2::margin()). debug Show debug rectangles. inherit.blank element inherit blank elements.

code: library(grid)  library(gdtools) font_set_liberation() #> Font set #>   sans:    Liberation Sans [liberation] #>   serif:   Liberation Serif [liberation] #>   mono:    Liberation Mono [liberation] #>   symbol:  Liberation Sans [liberation] #>   4 HTML dependencies flextable::set_flextable_defaults(   font.size = 12,   font.family = "Liberation Sans" )  if (require(ggiraph, quietly = TRUE)) {   x <- girafe(     width_svg = 3,     height_svg = 1,     bg = "wheat",     options = list(opts_sizing(rescale = FALSE)),     code = {       # Simple markdown (uses flextable defaults)       gr <- md_grob("This is **bold** and *italic* text.")       grid.newpage()       grid.draw(gr)     },     dependencies = list(       liberationsansHtmlDependency()     )   )    print(x)    x <- girafe(     width_svg = 3,     height_svg = 1,     bg = "wheat",     options = list(opts_sizing(rescale = FALSE)),     code = {       # Customize with text_props (standalone, no flextable dependency)       props <- default_text_props(font_size = 14, font_color = "navy")       gr2 <- md_grob("Code example: `print(x)`", text_props = props)       grid.newpage()       grid.draw(gr2)     },     dependencies = list(       liberationsansHtmlDependency()     )   )    print(x) }

what: Patchwork Annotation with Rich Text — munch_annotation
title: Patchwork Annotation with Rich Text — munch_annotation
text: replacement patchwork::plot_annotation() supports element_chunks() element_md() title, subtitle, /caption combined patchwork plot. text argument accepts: element_chunks() element_md() object — rendered rich text auto-wrapping; formatting options (hjust, lineheight, margin, etc.) set inside element call. bare flextable::as_paragraph() object — wrapped element_chunks() default settings. plain character string — passed unchanged. NULL — element omitted. Patchwork renders annotation element non-NULL string provided patchwork::plot_annotation(). element/chunks-based inputs, munch_annotation supplies invisible sentinel string patchwork creates layout row, element_chunks() element_md() handles actual rendering using stored content (label ignored).
